title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lewisville, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lewisville, OH
metaDescription: Lewisville sits in Monroe County, in Ohio's Utica/Point Pleasant core along the Ohio River. See what that means for your mineral interest value.
heroLead: Lewisville sits in Monroe County near the Ohio River, in a stretch of the state where farm families have watched drilling activity ebb and flow for well over a decade.
intro: Lewisville is a small village in Monroe County, one of the more consistently active counties in the Utica/Point Pleasant core since the play's early years. Land here was farmed for generations before drilling arrived, and the county's river-valley position has also meant occasional overlap with older conventional oil history and, given proximity to West Virginia, some Marcellus interest as well.

sections.heading: Monroe County's steady core activity near Lewisville
paragraphs: Monroe County has hosted consistent horizontal development for over a decade, and Lewisville sits within that broader activity corridor. A mineral owner here can often find comparable well data from the surrounding area even if their specific tract hasn't been drilled directly, which helps ground a valuation conversation in real numbers.

sections.heading: Farm severances and multi-generation heirship
paragraphs: Most mineral reservations around Lewisville trace back to simple farm deeds, and after multiple generations of inheritance, ownership is often split among several descendants, each holding a fractional share. A title search through the Monroe County Recorder's office in Woodsfield will confirm your exact current decimal interest and whether it's tied to a producing unit.

faqs.question: Is Lewisville in an actively producing part of Monroe County?
faqs.answer: Monroe County has seen consistent Utica development, and many tracts near Lewisville sit within that activity, though results vary by specific spacing unit.

faqs.question: Could my interest be tied to Marcellus activity given proximity to West Virginia?
faqs.answer: It's possible for some river-valley tracts, though which formation applies depends on the specific well and lease, so checking your documents directly is the way to confirm.

faqs.question: How do I confirm my exact share among multiple heirs?
faqs.answer: A title search tracing the original severance deed through every subsequent inheritance will confirm your current fractional interest relative to the other heirs.

faqs.question: What documents should I gather before contacting a buyer?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease or division order, and recent royalty statements if you have them, which together establish your net mineral acres and current decimal interest.

faqs.question: What if my family's minerals have never generated a royalty check?
faqs.answer: Your interest may sit in a unit that hasn't started producing, or you may not be properly identified on the current division order. A title search will clarify which situation applies.

faqs.question: Do I need to sell my entire interest, or can I sell just a portion?
faqs.answer: Most owners can sell all or part of their net mineral acres, sometimes limiting a sale to the interest under one specific well while retaining the rest.
